title: ERP rollout: lessons learned (2023)
summary: Internal review of AeroTech's last major system rollout.
points: The rollout went live on schedule and met its technical milestones.
Engineering output fell by about 20% for six months; the dip was not in the budget.
The business case assumed benefits within three months; they took more than a year to appear.

title: Engineering IT risk register
summary: The current risk register for engineering systems.
points: Rated high: CATIA V5 entering sustaining support, with future operating system compatibility unconfirmed.
Rated medium: unsupported workstation builds kept only to run older V5 add-ins.
Rated low: licence server hardware nearing end of life.

title: Airbus supplier performance review
summary: Airbus's annual review of AeroTech as a supplier.
points: On-time delivery: 97%, rated strong. Delivery performance during supplier change programmes will be monitored closely.
Digital collaboration maturity: rated developing, below the leading suppliers.
Airbus does not prescribe suppliers' CAD tools; it assesses the capability they enable.

title: Competitor activity briefing
summary: A summary of competing tier-2 aerospace suppliers.
points: Three of five tracked competitors announced digital engineering investments since 2024.
Two now offer customers model-based definition (MBD) data as standard.
Bid debrief: the 2025 work package AeroTech lost cited MBD capability as a factor.

title: Engineering workforce profile
summary: Headcount, age profile and recruitment data for the 220 engineering users.
points: Eight of the 25 most experienced CATIA engineers are eligible to retire within five years.
Training spend rose 30% over two years, yet graduate offer acceptance fell from 90% to 70%.
No documented succession plan exists for specialist CAD and CAM roles.
